overview: Guatemala is a country in Central America, south of Mexico. Its capital, Guatemala City, is the largest city in Central America. Guatemala was at the heart of the ancient Maya civilisation, and ruined cities such as Tikal can still be visited. Many Guatemalans today are Maya and speak Mayan languages as well as Spanish.

geography.text: A chain of volcanoes runs through Guatemala's highlands, some of them still active, such as Volcán de Fuego. Lake Atitlán, ringed by volcanoes, is one of the most famous lakes in the Americas. The north, called Petén, is lowland covered in tropical forest, and the country has coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean.

history.text: Guatemala was a heartland of the Maya, who built great cities such as Tikal. Spain conquered it in the 1520s, and it became independent in 1821. A US-backed coup in 1954 was followed by a civil war from 1960 to 1996, in which some 200,000 people, most of them Maya, were killed or disappeared.

government.text: Guatemala is a presidential republic. The President is elected for a single four-year term. Its Congress has one chamber. In 2023 voters elected Bernardo Arévalo, an anti-corruption candidate, despite attempts by prosecutors to stop him taking office.

economy.text: Guatemala has the largest economy in Central America. It exports coffee, bananas, cardamom, sugar and clothing; it is the world's biggest exporter of cardamom. Money sent home by Guatemalans in the United States makes up about a fifth of the economy.

culture.text: More than 40% of Guatemalans are Maya, and over 20 Mayan languages are spoken. Maya women weave colourful clothing whose patterns show their home village. Tikal, a vast Maya city in the jungle, is a UNESCO site.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. In 2012 Erick Barrondo won Guatemala's first Olympic medal, a silver in race walking, and shooter Adriana Ruano won its first gold in 2024.

items.text: Adriana Ruano won Olympic gold in trap shooting.

didYouKnow: Guatemala has 37 volcanoes, three of them active.
Chocolate was drunk by the Maya in Guatemala more than 2,500 years ago.
